newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, May 10 Initial Claims from 319,000 and May 3 from 350,000; May 10 Four-Week Average from 333,500 and May 3 from 336,750; May 3 Continued Claims from 2,314,000 and April 26 from 2,291,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 324,000 in the May 17 week.
The department said nine states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended May 10, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were New York, with 6,336 fewer jobless claims, North Dakota with 2,231, Minnesota with 1,841, Kentucky with 1,758 and New Jersey with 1,399.

Despite the drop in North Dakota's claims activity, claims in that state were still higher than normal due to flooding, the department said. In Minnesota, more than 700 claims were reported to be flood related.

Kentucky reported fewer layoffs in the rubber industry, while New Jersey said it had fewer layoffs in the transportation, trade and service industries, and in manufacturing. New York provided no comment.
Labor said four states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the May 10 week.
They were Pennsylvania, with 1,582 additional claims filings, Tennessee with 1,452, Ohio with 1,064 and Alabama with 1,011.
Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the trade, service, chemical and fabricated metals industries.

Tennessee said it had layoffs in the construction, service, food, apparel, and electronic equipment industries, and in manufacturing. Alabama reported layoffs in the textile and electrical machinery industries. Ohio gave no explanation.
